editorial:
Imagine being in a relationship where one person is totally shut off from their emotions. That is exactly what you get with Vincent and Olivier. Vincent is a bit of a mystery; he pushes people away and avoids being close, even though he is with Olivier. To try and spice things up and break through Vincent's walls, the couple starts looking for a third partner to join them. It feels like a heavy, moody ride from the start, focusing on how hard it is to love someone who is stuck in their own head. You will see a lot of tension as Olivier tries his best to help Vincent face the things he has been hiding for years.

What really makes this story work is the strange job Vincent has. He listens to recordings from plane crashes, which is a huge clue about why he is so broken inside. The acting is strong, and the way the story unfolds feels like a slow burn that eventually pays off. It is not an action movie, so if you like fast plots, this might feel slow. However, if you enjoy deep character studies, you should definitely check it out.
endingExplained: At the end, Vincent finally connects the dots between his job and his past. He realizes that listening to plane crashes was his way of staying stuck in the day his father died. By facing this pain with Olivier's help, he finally breaks his emotional shell. The movie wraps up with Vincent letting go of his grief, allowing him to finally be honest and open in his relationship instead of hiding behind his walls.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories about trauma and relationships.
